entry.reverseConfirmBody: A correction is always an additional entry: TILL posts a reversal with debit and credit swapped. The original entry stays in the journal unchanged, both entries remain visible, and the two cancel each other out.
entry.deleteConfirmBody: The draft and its lines are removed for good. A draft has never been posted, so nothing in the books changes, but the draft itself cannot be recovered.
entry.discardConfirmBody: What you entered in this entry is not saved yet and will be lost.

ownedBy.reverse_payment: This entry belongs to a payment: reverse the payment under Payments.
ownedBy.reopen_bank_line_done: This entry came from a bank line and is already reversed. Decide the line under Bank.
ownedBy.vat_settlement_reverse: This entry belongs to a VAT settlement: reverse the settlement under VAT.
ownedBy.accrual_reverse: This entry belongs to an accrual: reverse the accrual under Periods.
ownedBy.provision_reverse: This entry belongs to a provision: reverse the provision under Periods.
ownedBy.provision_release_reverse: This entry releases a provision: take the release back under Periods.
ownedBy.fx_revaluation_reverse: This entry belongs to a currency revaluation: reverse the revaluation under Foreign currency.
ownedBy.void_vendor_bill: This entry belongs to a vendor bill: void the bill under Vendor bills.
ownedBy.transition_document: This entry belongs to an invoice or credit note: cancel the document under Documents.
ownedBy.asset_depreciation_run_reverse: This entry belongs to a depreciation run: reverse the run in the Asset register.
ownedBy.inventory_valuation_reverse: This entry belongs to an inventory valuation: reverse the valuation run under Valuation runs.

Journal.title: Journal
Journal.body:
The journal is the immutable list of every entry posted in TILL for this workspace. Posted entries are never rewritten: a correction is always a reversing entry that cancels the mistake visibly.

Every line carries its account, its amount and, where VAT is involved, its tax code. The return is later computed from that code.

A taken-over prior-system journal appears beside it as its own archive. It is not part of the live chain of records.
